decision: Convene a cross-company engineering conference on cables and print its proceedings without publishing them
state_before: cable practice varied by company and supplier; insulation and crosstalk failures absorbed locally
information_available: their own tests; how thin the published literature was
unknowns: who authorised it; cost; circulation; whether it changed specifications
alternatives: meet informally and record nothing; write to each company separately
constraints: no print evidence of the trade-off
rationale: 'we will have in the report of this meeting a large amount of valuable data preserved in a permanent form available for future reference'
expected_result: a shared basis for cable specification
actual_result: not assessable in-window; the document survives as bytes and is the earliest held record of the registrant acting

decision: Adopt the twisted-pair underground conductor, accepting the abandonment of the existing underground plant
state_before: an installed underground plant of unquantified value
information_available: comparative performance of types in service
unknowns: who authorised; the amount abandoned; whether it was contested
constraints: capital at risk; service continuity during changeover
rationale: the new type was necessary for the system as it came to exist
expected_result: a plant capable of long underground circuits
actual_result: the 1902-1913 loading programme proceeded on it (all later statements by the same registrant)
confidence: Low as to agency; Medium that the claim is made

decision: Design and lay progressively longer loaded underground sections toward a Washington-Boston through route
state_before: a 90-mile cable usable only between New York and Philadelphia
information_available: its own transmission calculations; storm damage to overhead routes
unknowns: internal debate; budget lines; rejected routes
constraints: copper cost; conduit access; weather exposure
rationale: to keep the seaboard cities from Washington to Boston from being 'isolated by storms destroying the overhead wires'
actual_result: achieved in 1913 on the company's own statement; 47 per cent of the through cable was short-haul type

decision: Accept all of the Attorney General's suggestions as a five-point course of action: dispose of the Western Union holding, cease acquiring control of competing telephone companies, and open toll interconnection on stated terms
state_before: a federal conflict the report itself calls national in scope; a Chicago action just conceded to receivers
information_available: sixty days of interviews; a California physical-connection holding in its favour; the ICC valuation newly begun
unknowns: the internal vote; whether any point was resisted; what was traded
constraints: pending federal action; public opinion; the valuation process
rationale: 'Wishing to put their affairs beyond fair criticism'
actual_result: accepted the same day by the Attorney General and endorsed by the President; the Western Union indebtedness of 4,000,000 was still a liability line at 1913-12-31, disposal unexecuted inside the window

decision: Continue the policy of investing the depreciation reserve in revenue-earning plant rather than holding it liquid or returning it
information_available: its own size; the 1914 construction estimate of about 56,000,000
unknowns: whether the policy was ever contested internally
alternatives: hold the reserve; pay it out
rationale: so that the public gets the use of plant on which 'no dividends or interest charges have to be earned'
actual_result: unchanged within the window; 70,183,000 was applied out of revenue in 1913

decision: Put an employees' pension, disability and insurance plan in effect and fund it against revenue
information_available: one year of experience; 16,054 cases of participation
unknowns: the decision date; the debate; the actuarial basis
alternatives: no plan; state or mutual provision
rationale: not stated in any held byte
expected_result: labour stability (an attribution this pass does not make)
actual_result: the combined system carried an Employees' Benefit Fund of 8,919,335 at 1913-12-31

decision: Decline to convert to automatic switching on the stated ground that its service quality was not demonstrated
state_before: a manual and semi-automatic plant changed several times in twenty-five years
information_available: its own study of every type of switchboard in use; that it held the necessary patent rights
unknowns: the internal cost comparison; whether engineers dissented
alternatives: adopt automatic; run both in parallel
constraints: subscriber behaviour under the automatic plan; the scale of the interurban network
rationale: dependability of service to the public
actual_result: no change inside the window; the post-window outcome is not used (§2 firewall)
